given: the full set of stock rows on the split schema
when: the down path runs to completion
then: every stock row is still present afterward with the same count and no row is dropped or duplicated

independence.rationale: prior ACs assert per-row schema and value reconstruction; this asserts the distinct no-data-loss outcome across the whole table, which can be failed independently by losing or duplicating rows even when the surviving rows' codes are reconstructed correctly.

architectural_notes: Infra: the whole-table row-count integrity contract for the downgrade, owned by the migration revision and the direct realization of PI3-rows-preserved (migration_reversible) and R1. The downgrade mutates columns in place (add + backfill + drop) with no DELETE and no re-INSERT, so cardinality is invariant across the rollback , the transactional boundary of the migration must leave every row present exactly once. Verified by a real-branch test capturing the row count before downgrade and asserting an identical count with no dropped or duplicated rows afterward (R4).
